whatItFakes: A month without a supplied housing event contributes zero event effect.
why: The standalone rule accepts only supplied events and needs a neutral result when none is present.
replacement: A sourced, recorded housing-event effect for every macro month.

whatItFakes: The layoff rule permits a one-dollar annual pay-coverage tolerance.
why: The legacy comparison includes this tolerance and golden equivalence retains it.
replacement: A sourced accounting or payroll tolerance for the modeled books.

whatItFakes: Missing town-average pay contributes zero to the hiring threshold.
why: The legacy helper defaults to zero when its caller has no town-pay record.
replacement: A recorded town-average pay amount or a tagged estimate for the relevant place.

whatItFakes: Persisted macro values retain six decimal places.
why: The port preserves legacy replay precision until a persisted-data precision contract is set.
replacement: A documented precision contract for macro values.

whatItFakes: Home-purchase prices round to $1,000 increments.
why: The legacy purchase calculation rounds this way for replay equivalence.
replacement: A sourced purchase-pricing and currency-rounding policy.

whatItFakes: New hires start at the 25th wage percentile and reach the 75th after 20 years.
why: The legacy rule has no sourced tenure curve and these values preserve current behavior.
replacement: A measured tenure-to-wage progression by occupation and place.

whatItFakes: The lifted job-rate rule accepts caller-supplied federal/state floor data; local floors are not represented.
why: The current source reader supplies no local minimum-wage data.
replacement: Place and effective-date keyed local minimum-wage facts.

whatItFakes: Policy-rate midpoint stands in for a 30-year mortgage-rate change.
why: The available macro records do not contain a consistent mortgage-rate series for every modeled place and month.
replacement: A supplied monthly mortgage-rate series for each place.

whatItFakes: Home-price growth has no housing-supply response term.
why: A place-level housing-supply elasticity is not present in the supplied facts.
replacement: A sourced supply-elasticity fact and its measured pass-through coefficient.

whatItFakes: The first recorded home-price index starts at 1.
why: The pure rule receives a finite macro series and needs a deterministic initial index.
replacement: A supplied, source-backed opening index level and date.

whatItFakes: Eviction disposition uses a four-month counsel threshold and a two-month threshold for a lenient judge.
why: The legacy disposition rule has no jurisdiction-specific outcome records; both are estimates retained for golden equivalence.
replacement: A sourced jurisdiction-specific case-outcome model with counsel and judge facts.

whatItFakes: Home-purchase financing uses a 360-month fixed term.
why: The legacy purchase rule uses this term and has no buyer-selected term fact.
replacement: A recorded loan term or sourced term distribution for the buyer and loan type.

whatItFakes: Banks do not extend new credit when national credit tightness is 0.75 or higher.
why: The legacy bank rule pauses new lines and growth after a national tightening threshold.
replacement: A sourced lender-wide credit availability measure and place-level applicability rule.

whatItFakes: A business borrows from the open town bank with the largest deposits; deposit ties use bank ID order.
why: Individual business-bank relationships are not supplied to the selection rule.
replacement: A recorded business-to-bank relationship and its active loan terms.

whatItFakes: A household head aged 60 or older selects owned outright tenure for a newly chosen home.
why: The legacy home selector uses age as a proxy and receives no recorded mortgage balance or paid-off status.
replacement: The household's recorded loan balance and home equity at the move date.

whatItFakes: Households of up to two select an apartment fallback; households of five or more may select a large house.
why: The legacy home selector uses fixed household-size bands without a sourced household-space model.
replacement: A household-space model fitted to recorded resident, room and dwelling facts.

whatItFakes: When a town spans multiple counties, its private employment mix weights each available county equally.

whatItFakes: Payroll aggregation considers late-recorded transfers only within 45 days before the selected period.
why: The legacy reader stops once it reaches outcomes older than its 45-day lookback.
replacement: A sourced, recorded payroll-transfer posting-lag distribution.

whatItFakes: Rejects operations when an intermediate product exceeds safe integer precision even when the final rational result or comparison could be represented.

replacement: Reviewed exact-integer arithmetic with an explicit persisted quantity bound.

whatItFakes: One-person households take a studio; other households use two people per bedroom, capped at four.
why: Preserve the legacy pure calculation and its missing-fact or estimated-mechanism behavior unchanged.
replacement: Recorded dwelling capacity/bedrooms and applicable occupancy rules.

whatItFakes: Subtracts 1e-9 before rounding the recorded affordable-home obligation upward.
why: Preserve the legacy pure calculation and its missing-fact or estimated-mechanism behavior unchanged.

whatItFakes: Multiplies a household-size mean by a region/national mean ratio as a joint cost estimate.

whatItFakes: Business operating income uses receipts less payroll and omits other operating costs.
